content: Genius, in truth, means little more than the faculty of perceiving in an unhabitual way.
author: William James
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. True art and creative work are not about clever technique; they demand total emotional skin in the game. When you create safely to please an audience or avoid criticism, the work feels hollow and bloodless.

In William James's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Pouring your genuine spirit, vulnerability, and raw lived experience into what you make is what gives it enduring life. The work that resonates across centuries is always the work created with unapologetic personal truth.
reflectionPrompt: What hidden motive, insecurity, or fear might be silently driving your recent reactions?
